Potential risk factors for increased violent behavior include:

1. *Use of corporal punishment as means of discipline*. As discussed earlier, this child is learning, at a very young age, to use violence to solve his problems.[7](#_ENREF_7)

The resident must make it clear to the parent that these symptoms are not completely explained by ADHD. The resident should then ask the parent to list other factors that might be contributing to the child’s behavior. One approach is to start by saying, *“I see ADHD in the clinic every week. This is does not sound like ADHD.”*
In this case, also recognize that the mother’s concern regarding her child’s behavior is considered a protective factor against future violent behavior.
SBP: Never tell an IPV victim that they should “*leave*” an abusive relationship. Leaving can be extremely dangerous for the victim and it must be coordinated with a skilled IPV counselor. You can call the national domestic violence hotline (1-800-799-SAFE).[14](#_ENREF_14)

This conversation should take place with the child outside of the room beginning at age 3.[18](#_ENREF_18) There is a concern that the child might repeat the content of your discussion with the perpetrator (father). Also, the mother may be less likely to disclose the details of her corporal punishment with the child in the room.
ICS: An effective approach might be to say, *“Children may pick up these kinds of violent behaviors from school, from their friends, from the television, or even from their homes. Sometimes if children see one parent hitting the other, they will replicate the same behaviors. Does this happen at your house?”* If the mother denies abuse you may try to challenge her with a gentle but direct statement, *“The last time that I saw a child like this it was because he witnessed his father hitting and cursing at his mother. Are you sure this has never happened to you?”* When parents disclose intimate partner violence to you it is important not to be judgmental.

Demonstrate empathy. Again, by ‘*being on her side’* the resident is much more likely to have the mother disclose the abuse that has happened to her.[15](#_ENREF_15) She is also more likely to be open to discussing alternatives to corporal punishment.
